question: What is another common name for a nosocomial infection?
explanation: Nosocomial infections are acquired specifically within healthcare settings during the delivery of care. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why are hospital-acquired infections considered a major challenge in clinical practice?

options.A: They always resolve without any medical care
options.B: They only occur in surgical theatre suites
options.C: They increase patient hospital stay duration
options.D: They are completely untreatable with drugs

explanation: These infections complicate recovery, leading to extended hospital admissions and higher treatment costs. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which component represents where a pathogen normally lives and multiplies?
explanation: A reservoir provides a suitable environment for microorganisms to survive, grow, and multiply. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h2)

question: What happens when a healthcare worker performs proper handwashing to break the infection cycle?

options.D: Infectious agent changes its DNA structure

explanation: Hand hygiene stops pathogens from moving from one surface or person to another. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which body fluid is excluded from standard precaution assumptions regarding infectious agents?
explanation: Standard precautions apply to all body fluids except sweat, unless it contains visible blood. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h3)

question: When should a nurse apply standard precautions in the ward?

options.A: Only when laboratory tests confirm a virus
options.B: When caring for every single patient
options.C: Only during surgical wound dressing changes
options.D: When visiting patients in the private wing

explanation: Standard precautions are universal and apply to all patient care activities regardless of infection status. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which respiratory protection is mandatory when caring for a patient with pulmonary tuberculosis?
explanation: Airborne pathogens like tuberculosis require high-filtration respirators to prevent inhaling small droplet nuclei. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h4)

question: A patient diagnosed with an infection spread through large respiratory droplets requires which precaution category?
explanation: Droplet precautions stop pathogens that travel short distances through moisture expelled during coughing or sneezing. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is the minimum recommended duration for washing visibly soiled hands with soap and water?
explanation: Friction from soap and water for nearly a minute is required to mechanically remove physical dirt and microbes. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why is soap and water preferred over alcohol hand rub when caring for a patient with Clostridium difficile?

options.A: Alcohol damages the hospital rubber gloves
options.B: Soap causes faster drying of skin oils
options.C: Soap has a pleasant fragrance for patients
options.D: Alcohol rubs do not destroy bacterial spores

explanation: Spore-forming organisms resist alcohol gels, requiring the physical washing action of soap and water. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the very first item a nurse should put on when donning personal protective equipment?
explanation: The gown is put on first to cover clothing, followed by respiratory protection, eye protection, and gloves. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why should gloves be removed first when taking off personal protective equipment after patient care?

options.A: The gown cannot be untied with gloves on
options.C: They carry the highest contamination load
options.D: They are the easiest item to tear apart

explanation: Gloves touch patients directly, accumulating the most pathogens, so removing them first minimizes spreading germs. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h6)

question: Where should the urine collection bag be positioned relative to the patient's bladder?

options.B: Hanging directly above the bed frame
options.D: Below the level of the bladder

explanation: Gravity drainage prevents contaminated urine from flowing backward into the sterile bladder. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h7)

question: A nurse needs to prevent a catheter-associated urinary tract infection. What action is most appropriate?

options.C: Disconnect the tubing daily for flushing
options.D: Raise the collection bag above the hips

explanation: Keeping the catheter tubing connected blocks external bacteria from entering the urinary tract. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h7)

question: Where should used hypodermic needles be disposed of immediately after injection?
explanation: Sharps containers prevent accidental needle-stick injuries to nurses and waste handlers. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h8)

question: Why is recapping used injection needles strongly discouraged in clinical settings?

options.A: It contaminates the inside of the needle barrel
options.B: It wastes valuable nursing shift time
options.C: It increases the risk of needle-stick injuries
options.D: It makes the syringe difficult to incinerate

explanation: Attempting to recap needles frequently leads to accidental punctures to the nurse's fingers. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h8)

question: Who should nurses report a sudden cluster of hospital infections to?
explanation: The infection control committee investigates outbreaks and implements facility-wide prevention strategies. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)

question: Why is early nursing surveillance vital for infection control in the ward?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.B: It reduces the cost of hospital building maintenance
options.C: It prevents patients from eating restricted foods
options.D: It stops local infections from turning into systemic sepsis

explanation: Spotting infection early allows for prompt medical intervention before the condition worsens. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)
